extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation, consisting of 1,825 diverse tasks to assess visual fidelity and interactive integrity.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involves aggregating candidates from various sources, followed by automated filtering to remove undesirable items. The data then undergoes a two-stage de-duplication process, prompt rewriting by experts and LLMs, and checklist generation with human refinement.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete items were dropped using automated filters.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidates sourced from expert showcases, open SVG and web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Tasks and checklists are initially drafted by LLMs and then refined and verified by human experts. A 10% manually curated seed is used to anchor calibration and serve as few-shot references.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was measured using Cohen's kappa for checklist calibration and pairwise agreement percentages for validating the automated referee against human judgments.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos was used for generating checklists, a lightweight classifier was used for tagging sub-categories, and Qwen2.5-VL-72B and Gemini-2.5-Pro were used as automated referees (MLLM-as-Judge).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing/Evaluation (Benchmark for evaluating LLMs on visual code generation and interactive visual artifacts)
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were rewritten by experts and LLMs to improve clarity and add diverse styles. The dataset was also calibrated post hoc based on model performance to enforce a specific 30%/40%/30% split for Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data underwent automated filtering to remove incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. De-duplication and contamination control were performed using MinHash, semantic similarity, and screenshot perceptual hashing. Underspecified items and tasks solvable by brittle hacks were pruned.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. We LLM-draft and then human-refine for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Experts rewrite for clarity/completeness/executability; LLM rewriting adds diverse styles; humans verify. Difficulty is assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce 30%/40%/30%; realized split 559/611/655

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Automated filters drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items... Two-stage filtering: (i) MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts... prune underspecified items.
